description: Source mirror L1 completeness: a full, resumable, GET-only sync of every relation the Portal Workbench reporting API catalog serves into a throwaway mirror file, the relations bound in ontology/schema/domains (the evaluation denominator) first, then one batch citation resolve. Three relations are read at a time (inside wb_api's five connections); relations the previous daily report names row-bound or paging-defective (defer_next_run, or counted above the mirror bound by mirror.relation_counts) stay in the denominator but are synced last, after the key-only reads. Relations the previous daily report's mirror.relation_counts names unstable (data_truth_defect on two consecutive daily runs) are never staged: they are read key-only by the no-store counter and leave the denominator. Pass = every stable bound relation complete (complete_bound_relation_count/bound_total, the completeness figure of decision 2026-10-02-capture-persistence), the catalog still serving at least 93 relations, every relation's counts recorded, and 5,000 handles resolved offline in under 3 s. The 93-relation figures (complete_relation_count, all_stable_served_complete, accounted_relation_count, accounted_equals_catalog) are recorded fields, never a failure. Output is counts, booleans, timings and relation names only; never a row value, key or citation.
notes: live-unverified until a live-check result exists. Daily cadence (python3 verify/live_verify.py --cadence daily): the 2026-10-01 hourly run took 1503 s of a 1500 s budget for 53/93 relations, so the full sync left the hourly suite. --workers 3: three relations are read at a time, each on its own fenced traversal and mirror connection (wb_api allows 5 connections; at most 4 workers). Retry-After honoured on 429/503; statement timeouts and HTTP 500 halve the page down to the floor, then retry with backoff; key-run-too-long/null-key 500s double it up to 5000 (the service's own remedy), never back to a size already proven too small or too large for the same cursor; row-too-large, a 500 at the limit and a cursor with no page size left between those two errors are a per-relation source_defect that never blocks the others. relation_outcomes[*] records every relation not captured (outcome, failure_class: budget | row_bound | paging_defect | source_defect | throttled | transport | contract | superseded | store_busy | internal_error (with exception_type, never the message), HTTP status, the service's error code, pages, rows, final page size, seconds); slowest_relations names the ten longest captures. A row_bound or paging_defect traversal is abandoned (never resumed into a stitched capture) and named in defer_next_run; every other interrupted traversal, budget cuts included, resumes from its last committed page on the next run. sync_seconds is the main sync only; key_only_seconds times the key-only reads of unstable relations and deferred_sync_seconds the late sync of deferred relations. Root cause of the five 1M-row gold relations (2026-10-01/02): petralabx/plx-customer-portal portal/scripts/etl-silver-to-gold.ts@c3ffda3 inserts every child row under a fresh cuid each ETL run, so ON CONFLICT (id) never fires and the tables grow per run; the keyset paging (services/workbench-api/src/core/query.mjs@c3ffda3) is correct, and the mirror now proves each page's cursor names that page's last key. The probe audience grants a service principal every served schema because it measures the mirror, not an employee's view. A relation that does not finish inside the budget is reported incomplete (in_progress_count) and the check fails rather than passing on partial data. complete_bound_relation_count/bound_total is the completeness figure the eval and the projection report (scripts.mirror_measure.completeness; bound_total excludes unstable relations, bound_declared_total does not); complete_relation_count/catalog_relation_count, all_stable_served_complete and accounted_relation_count/accounted_equals_catalog stay secondary: recorded, not gated (an unbound relation left incomplete never fails the check). --previous-report={daily_report} is the runner's --daily-report (results/daily/latest.json); without it no relation is unstable and the probe behaves as before. Relations whose true count exceeds the mirror's max_rows_per_relation are measured by mirror.relation_counts. Source deletions (ING-09): rows_deleted_in_source_total and soft_deleted_rows (per relation whose catalog carries a soft-delete column declared in integrations/source_mirror_ingest.json soft_delete_rules; relation names and counts only) count the distinct record keys the source soft-deleted (deleted_in_source) in this run, and rows_missing_total the distinct keys missing from it (a duplicate-key run is one record; despite the rows_ names, rows_current_total counts held rows, duplicates and soft-deleted ones included); soft_delete_relation_count >= 1 proves the declaration still matches the live catalog. Live-pending until a live-check result records them. Session state (verify/live_verify.py): the session producer of {session_state}/mirror.sqlite: the ontology probes (ontology.projection, ontology.traverse, ontology.mentions, workspace.object_view) require this spec and top its mirror up incrementally in the same runner session instead of a cold sync each (daily run 4ea6073: about 8 checks each re-synced the Portal, ~1,538 s apiece). Its own check is unchanged: a session starts with an empty directory. Typed gaps: a bound relation the live catalog lists but does not serve (run outcome unavailable) stays in bound_incomplete (all_bound_complete false, complete_when unmet) and is named in blocked_upstream (cause relation_unavailable); bound_incomplete_untyped holds every bound relation incomplete any other way. With only typed parts missing and expect_blocked met (every other expectation, bound_incomplete_untyped empty) the check is blocked relation_unavailable, never a pass; any untyped incomplete bound relation (budget, row bound, paging defect, failure) is a fail.
